result.area: O-07 odoo-pakka-khata-design: getting manager-approved formal postings out of the app (kacha khata) into Odoo (pakka khata), correctly and idempotently, without assuming a Custom plan

hypothesis_ranking.discriminating_test: In the owner's Odoo test company (any plan), import a 2-move journal-entry CSV with External IDs twice, and confirm the second import updates the draft moves rather than duplicating them (R-02 F10: the importer modifies a record when the External ID already exists). Then post one move and re-import, and confirm the import refuses with an error instead of creating a duplicate.

Payment and negotiate events carry no payload (service.py:1478-1484, 1400; S16), so the event stream cannot rebuild a paisa-exact posting. On top of that, seq comes from a Sequence at flush (models.py:56,271) while the drain reads seq > last_seq (service.py:509-516). Test: open two transactions, flush an event in T1 (lower seq), commit T2 (higher seq), run run_dispatch_once, then commit T1. T1's event is never delivered.

After the window's export record exists, add a staff_ledger row with occurred_on inside an already-exported window (a back-entry the model explicitly allows, attendance/models.py:433-436) and re-run. The clone returns the existing record (attendance/service.py:1249-1253), so the row appears in no export, ever.

bill_original_paisa is overwritten on resubmit (service.py:1282) and a payment void stores no time (models.py:494-496). Invoices are safe only at close, because negotiate (1385) and completion (1155) refuse closed jobs and closed is terminal. Payments and ledger rows can be derived, but void dates cannot. Check whether any non-closed bill figure can be reconstructed from job_event alone: it cannot (text in whole rupees only).

A set-difference stager reads job_payment / closed jobs / staff_ledger through the jobs and attendance service.py and anti-joins against posting (source_kind, source_id, rev). The only write-path change is void_payment stamping the new voided_at/voided_by columns. Check that lint-imports passes with one new accounting→jobs and accounting→attendance service edge and no reverse edge.

findings.title: No approval boundary or record of what reached the formal books
findings.claim: No table or column records which money facts were sent to formal books or their state when sent, and the sources change in place, so re-exporting a window after a payment void yields a different file than the one already imported, with nothing to show what changed.
findings.failing_condition: A payment is exported, then a manager voids it: job_payment.voided flips in place (no new row), so a regenerated export silently drops the original and no reversal is ever produced.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:465-497 — JobPayment has no external_ref/posted_at/export id; voided and void_reason are in-place columns
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1507-1508 — payment.voided = True / payment.void_reason = reason
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1282 — row.bill_original_paisa = original (overwritten on every permitted resubmit)
backend/app/features/attendance/models.py:365-387 — the only export record (payroll_export) has no per-row ids, totals or checksum
findings.impact: The owner's 'total accounting, nothing missing' requirement cannot be met or audited: the formal books cannot be reconciled with the operational cash system, and a void after export leaves Odoo overstated with no trace.
findings.fix_sketch: Migration 0047 adds an immutable posting snapshot table (source_kind, source_id, rev, external_id UNIQUE, snapshot + sha256, amount_minor > 0, lines), an append-only posting_decision and posting_attempt, and posting_export with a manifest. A void becomes a reversal posting, never an edit (see design).

findings.title: Cloning run_weekly_export's return-existing-window shape drops late facts
findings.claim: run_weekly_export returns the existing record untouched once a (shop, window) export exists, so a posting export keyed by the facts' own dates would never include a fact that arrives after its window was exported: a back-dated staff_ledger row, a later void, or a late-synced offline payment.
findings.failing_condition: On Monday a manager records Friday's advance (occurred_on = last week) after Sunday's export ran. A re-run returns the existing record and the advance is in no export.
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1249-1253 — existing = await self._repo.get_export_for_window(...); if existing is not None: return existing
backend/app/features/attendance/models.py:433-436 — occurred_on differs from created_at 'whenever a manager back-enters Friday's advance on Monday'
docs/requirements-2026-07-gap-analysis.md:107-113 — Phase 1 says clone run_weekly_export, window-keyed
findings.impact: Under-reporting by construction: every correction or late fact lands in no formal export. The reconciliation delta would grow without an owner.
findings.fix_sketch: Key the export window on posting decided_at (approval time), not on the fact date. Each approved posting is claimed by exactly one export (UPDATE ... SET export_id WHERE export_id IS NULL), and the accounting_date column carries the fact's own date. A late fact goes into the next export.

findings.title: Abandon is an ungated one-tap exit for a billed, paid job
findings.claim: Any authenticated principal can abandon an open, waiting or ready job through the ungated /transition route, which closes it with abandoned=True even when it carries a bill and payments. A posting rule that excludes abandoned jobs from invoicing would make under-reporting a single tap.
findings.failing_condition: A tech completes a job (bill generated), collects cash, then POSTs /api/jobs/{id}/transition {action:'abandon', reason:'x'}. The job closes abandoned and an invoice rule like 'closed AND NOT abandoned' never stages it.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/router.py:194-198 — '/{job_id}/transition' has no dependencies=[Depends(require_manager)]
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:757 — "abandon": ("open", "waiting", "ready")
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1110-1116 — values = {status: closed, closed_at: now, abandoned: True, abandon_reason}
findings.impact: Revenue can leave the formal books through a lifecycle action that needs no manager and no bill reversal.
findings.fix_sketch: The stager stages an invoice for every closed job with a bill, abandoned or not, flagged 'abandoned'. Keeping it out of the books needs a typed manager rejection that shows in the reconciliation delta. Separately, consider manager-gating abandon when bill_original_paisa is set or a non-voided payment exists.

findings.title: Any principal can negotiate a bill down to zero
findings.claim: NegotiateRequest accepts amount_paisa >= 0 and the negotiate route has no manager gate, so any technician can set the payable figure an accrual invoice would post to Rs 0 before close.
findings.failing_condition: A tech POSTs /api/jobs/{id}/bill/negotiate {amount_paisa: 0} on a Rs 5,000 bill. bill_negotiated_paisa = 0 takes precedence in _payable_paisa, and the invoice posts Rs 0 with no approval.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/schemas.py:145-147 — amount_paisa: int = Field(..., ge=0)
backend/app/features/jobs/router.py:304-331 — negotiate route takes CurrentPrincipal, no require_manager
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1385-1392 — only refuses a closed job or a missing bill
backend/app/features/customer_messaging/service.py:78-83 — negotiated wins over original
findings.impact: The cheapest path to a smaller formal-books figure is a technician-side action with no reason required.
findings.fix_sketch: The invoice posting always carries the gross original lines plus an explicit sales_discount line (original − payable), flagged negotiated_below_original. Reconciliation itemises discounts by actor. Owner decision: require a manager (or a reason) for negotiations below a threshold.

findings.title: A payment void has no timestamp, and the server allows it after close
findings.claim: void_payment never checks the job's status and stores no voided_at or voided_by, so a void made weeks after close cannot be dated to its accounting period except by fuzzy-matching job_event text.
findings.failing_condition: A manager voids a payment on a job closed last month via POST /payments/{id}/void (the web UI hides the button on closed jobs, but the API accepts it). The reversal has no void date on any row.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1489-1520 — no row.status check; payment.voided = True / payment.void_reason = reason
backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:494-496 — voided and void_reason only; no voided_at/voided_by
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1509-1515 — the void event text carries the reason but no payment id or amount
findings.impact: Reversal postings land in the wrong period, or carry an unknown date, once the period is locked in Odoo.
findings.fix_sketch: 0047 adds job_payment.voided_at timestamptz NULL and voided_by varchar(64) NULL (FK technician, NOT VALID + VALIDATE in the same migration because the new column is all NULL), and void_payment stamps both. Historical rows get a dry-run-default backfill script in backend/scripts/ that matches a job's single 'Payment voided — ' event. Otherwise the reversal is dated at staging and flagged void_date_unknown.

findings.title: The job_event seq cursor can permanently skip a late-committing event
findings.claim: job_event.seq is drawn from a Postgres sequence at flush and run_dispatch_once reads only seq > cursor.last_seq, so an event whose transaction commits after a higher-seq event has been drained is skipped permanently. An erp consumer built on this cursor would silently lose postings.
findings.failing_condition: Request A flushes its event (seq 101) and stalls before commit, request B commits seq 102, the dispatcher drains to last_seq = 102, then A commits. seq 101 is never selected.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:56 — job_event_seq = Sequence("job_event_seq", ...)
backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:269-271 — the sequence is the client-side default for seq
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:509-516 — select(JobEvent).where(JobEvent.seq > cursor.last_seq).order_by(JobEvent.seq)
backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:229-230 — docstring claims 'gap-free global ordering key'
findings.impact: A WhatsApp nudge is missed today (dispatcher default OFF). For a journal feed it would be an unnoticed missing entry.
findings.fix_sketch: Do not build the ERP feed on job_event. The stager is a state-based anti-join (source rows without a posting), which is immune to commit order. posting.seq is assigned under a per-shop pg_advisory_xact_lock held to commit (the staff_ledger_chain pattern), so it is gapless and commit-ordered. Do not seed an 'erp' dispatch_cursor row.

findings.title: Offline-queued payments are dated at sync time, not collection time
findings.claim: PaymentRequest carries no capture timestamp and job_payment.recorded_at is the server's now(), so a payment the phone's outbox replays after a month boundary is dated, and would be posted, in the wrong accounting period.
findings.failing_condition: A tech logs cash offline at 23:30 on the 31st and the outbox syncs on the 1st: recorded_at (and so the posting's accounting_date) is the 1st.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/schemas.py:153-159 — PaymentRequest has amount_paisa, method, client_id only
backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:491-493 — recorded_at server_default now()
technician-app/src/lib/outboxSync.ts:115-117 — case "payment": jobsApi.logPayment(item.jobId, p.amountPaisa, p.method, p.clientId)
findings.impact: Period misstatement at month and year end. Small amounts, but a known source of reconciliation noise.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an optional captured_at to PaymentRequest, trust-windowed like pings (about 48 h back / 2 min forward), stored as job_payment.captured_at. accounting_date = captured_at when present, else recorded_at, flagged offline_dated. Deployed APKs keep the fallback.

findings.title: The job_payment amount CHECK is still NOT VALID; history may hold amounts <= 0
findings.claim: The job_payment_amount_positive CHECK from 0038 was never validated (the VALIDATE exists only as a docstring follow-up), so historical payment rows may hold amount_paisa <= 0, and staging them would violate a posting table's amount_minor > 0 CHECK.
findings.failing_condition: A pre-0038 row with amount_paisa = 0 (or negative) exists. The stager's INSERT into posting fails and, if unhandled, wedges every later staging run.
evidence: backend/alembic/versions/0038_job_payment_amount_guard.py:15-28 — 'Created NOT VALID deliberately' ... follow-up 'VALIDATE CONSTRAINT' in the docstring
backend/alembic/versions/0038_job_payment_amount_guard.py:51 — CHECK (amount_paisa > 0) NOT VALID
grep: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT job_payment_amount_positive appears only in 0038's docstring
findings.impact: A poison row stops the stager, or gets dropped silently if handled carelessly.
findings.fix_sketch: The stager skips source rows that violate posting CHECKs, writes an app_event alarm, and counts them in reconciliation's 'unpostable' bucket. 0048 (separate deploy, after the audit SELECT) VALIDATEs the constraint.

findings.title: A manager correction of a negotiated bill leaves the payable figure stale
findings.claim: A manager completion resubmit on a negotiated bill rewrites bill_original_paisa but leaves bill_negotiated_paisa unchanged, so the payable figure ignores the correction and original − payable can go negative.
findings.failing_condition: Bill Rs 5,000 negotiated to Rs 4,500, then a manager resubmits adding a forgotten Rs 2,000 part. Original becomes Rs 7,000 while payable stays Rs 4,500, and the correction has no effect on what is billed or posted.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1158-1159 — the freeze applies only when not is_manager
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1282-1283 — bill_original_paisa = original; bill_status stays 'negotiated' when bill_negotiated_paisa is not None
backend/app/features/customer_messaging/service.py:81-83 — negotiated wins
findings.impact: The invoice posting must handle a discount line of either sign. The manager may believe a correction took effect when it did not.
findings.fix_sketch: The posting lines compute discount = original − payable and put it on the debit side if positive or the credit side if negative, flagged negotiated_stale. Separately, surface 'negotiated figure predates the last correction' in the bill UI, or clear the negotiation on a manager correction (owner call).

findings.title: The export record is check-then-insert, with the object written before the record
findings.claim: run_weekly_export does a read-then-insert with no lock, and add_export has no IntegrityError recovery, so two concurrent runs both write the storage object and the loser surfaces a unique-violation 500. A crash between put_bytes and commit leaves an object without a record.
findings.failing_condition: The Sunday scheduler run overlaps an on-demand run for the same window.
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1249-1270 — get_export_for_window ... self._storage.put_bytes(...) ... add_export(...)
backend/app/features/attendance/repository.py:439-457 — add_export: session.add + flush, no IntegrityError handling
backend/app/features/attendance/models.py:371-373 — UNIQUE(shop_id, from_date, to_date)
findings.impact: Harmless for payroll. For a posting export it could produce two different downloadable byte sets for one window.
findings.fix_sketch: The posting exporter takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(shop, 'posting_export') and inserts the record first (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING). It builds deterministic bytes (postings ordered by seq) at a deterministic path, stores the sha256 on the record, and commits. A retry regenerates identical bytes.

findings.title: External IDs must not derive from seqs, tokens or seeded slugs
findings.claim: Odoo's importer updates whatever record already holds an External ID. Any ID built from a per-database counter (posting seq, job token, chain seq) or a seeded slug collides after a fresh database rebuild, where sequences restart at 1 and t1..t5/m1 recur (S14), and the next import silently overwrites previously imported moves.
findings.failing_condition: Production is gone and a fresh self-hosted DB starts at chain/posting seq 1. A CSV with External ID 'fixflow_posting_1' re-imports over last year's move with that ID.
evidence: backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1370-1373 — seq = head[0] + 1 if head is not None else 1 (restarts on an empty DB)
backend/app/features/jobs/models.py:118 — job.token is unique only within this database
R-02 F10 — the importer modifies existing records on a matching External ID, and External IDs are unique across all objects
findings.impact: Silent corruption of the formal books from a routine rebuild.
findings.fix_sketch: external_id = 'fixflow_<kind>_<source_uuid hex32>[_rev<n>|_x<n>]', where the source UUID comes from gen_random_uuid (job_payment.id, job.id, staff_ledger.id). Line IDs are '<move_xid>_l<n>'. Partners use customer UUIDs, and techs use '<shop>_<tech_id>' only after the owner confirms that tech-id reuse means the same person.

findings.title: The manifest cannot be a row inside the import CSV
findings.claim: The gap analysis puts a manifest line carrying count and sum inside the batch CSV, but Odoo's importer would treat any extra row as a record (or reject the file), so the manifest must be a separate file.
findings.failing_condition: The manager uploads the export CSV with a trailing 'MANIFEST,count,sum' row into Odoo's journal-entry import.
evidence: docs/requirements-2026-07-gap-analysis.md:111-112 — 'a manifest line carries count + sum for eyeball reconciliation'
R-02 F10 — import semantics are per-row record create/update
findings.impact: Either the import fails, or a junk record or line is created in the formal books.
findings.fix_sketch: Write manifest.json plus manifest.csv beside the import CSV in the export folder. The posting_export record stores the counts, Σdebit, Σcredit, the CSV sha256 and the rejected/pending sums for the same window.

findings.title: The PaymentRail Protocol is synchronous; an Odoo transport must not copy that
findings.claim: PaymentRail.disburse is a plain def called inside async service code, so an HTTP-backed Odoo transport cloned from it would block the event loop for the length of each one-call-per-second Odoo request.
findings.failing_condition: An OdooJson2Transport.push implemented as a sync httpx call inside the scheduler's async job stalls every API request served by that replica for each call.
evidence: backend/app/core/payment_rail.py:47-52 — def disburse(self, *, amount_minor, currency, idempotency_key) -> DisbursementResult (sync)
backend/app/features/attendance/service.py:1700-1707 — result = self._rail.disburse(...) called without await inside an async method
findings.impact: Latency spikes on the API while ERP pushes run.
findings.fix_sketch: core/posting_transport.py defines an async Protocol (async def find(xid), async def push(snapshot)) with typed DefinitiveTransportError, AmbiguousTransportError and TransportAuthError. It mirrors PaymentRail's narrow-surface and idempotency_key=external_id contract, not its sync signature.

findings.title: No settings keys exist for posting, the account map or ERP
findings.claim: The shop_setting registry has only the two money rates and the five advance keys, so there is nowhere to record the posting start date, cash-vs-accrual basis, account-code mapping, journals, lag threshold or API-key expiry. Nothing may write an unregistered key.
findings.failing_condition: Any attempt to configure the export through PUT /api/shop/settings with an unregistered key is refused.
evidence: backend/app/features/tenancy/specs.py:3-6 — 'nothing may write a key that is not registered here'
backend/app/features/tenancy/specs.py:30-38 — registered keys: labour/fuel rates + five advance keys
findings.impact: Policy would get hard-coded or put in env by default. That is the 'placeholder becomes policy' failure the working agreement forbids.
findings.fix_sketch: Register (all defaulting to unset or off): posting_start_date, posting_basis, account_code_<role> for each role, journal_code_<sales|cash|payroll>, posting_lag_alert_hours, odoo_api_key_expires_on. Approval is refused while any role used by a posting is unmapped. Secrets stay in env.

findings.title: Payment dedupe ignores job and amount
findings.claim: log_payment dedupes on client_id alone, so a request that reuses an existing client_id with a different job or amount returns success without writing anything, and the operational total diverges from what the caller believes it logged.
findings.failing_condition: A client bug reuses a client_id from job A on job B. The response is a 200 JobDetail for B with no new payment row.
evidence: backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1457-1459 — existing = await self._repo.get_payment_by_client(client_id); if existing is None: ...
backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:1486-1487 — falls through to return the detail with no mismatch check
findings.impact: A low-probability silent loss of a cash entry. Postings stay consistent with the table but the table is wrong.
findings.fix_sketch: When existing.job_id != row.id or existing.amount_paisa != amount_paisa, raise a 409 (a definitive 4xx, so the phone parks it as visible-failed rather than dropping it).

backlog.title: Advance auto-approve passes actor='auto' into staff_ledger.recorded_by (FK technician): an auto-disbursed advance cannot write its ledger row, so it never reaches postings
Advance disbursement hardcodes currency='PKR'; the posting snapshot must take shop.currency instead
Payroll CSV re-run returns the existing record, so attendance adjustments made after Sunday's export never reach any payroll export (same shape as O07-F2, current defect; adjustments code not read)
job_payment has no shop_id; the posting stager has to join via job.shop_id (add column NOT VALID FK in 0048)
job_payment.recorded_by has no FK to technician (populated human data → NOT VALID in 0048, VALIDATE 0049 after orphan audit)
Gap-analysis R2 says the erp cursor row already exists; it does not (0046 seeds only whatsapp). Correct the doc and record that the posting design needs no cursor row
JobEvent docstring claims seq is gap-free; it is sequence-allocated and not commit-ordered
Four-eyes approval (recorder != approver) is impossible with a single manager (m1); posting approval is self-approval until a second manager exists
Payment logging is allowed on a closed job (log_payment has no status check), so postings must accept payments dated after the invoice

result.design:
PRINCIPLE. Postings are a downstream, append-only projection of the operational ledgers (kacha khata). Odoo (pakka khata) never feeds back. A new backend slice, backend/app/features/accounting/ (router → service → repository, models, schemas, tests), owns the projection. It reads jobs and attendance only through their service.py; add import-linter edges accounting→jobs.service and accounting→attendance.service, never the reverse. The only change to an existing write path is void_payment stamping voided_at/voided_by. Postings are found by a STATE-BASED stager (source rows with no posting, via anti-join), never by the job_event cursor. Payment and negotiate events carry no amounts or ids (S16), and seq is not commit-ordered (O07-F6). Every posting is an immutable snapshot. A correction is always a reversal plus a new revision, never an update, because Odoo refuses to modify a posted move and a changed External ID duplicates.

(1) RECORD SET AND STABLE IDENTIFIERS
- job_payment (id uuid = source_id; client_id; amount_paisa; method; recorded_at; voided/void_reason, plus voided_at/voided_by from 0047) → 'payment' posting, and 'payment_reversal' on void.
- job (id uuid; token for human reference only; status closed; closed_at; abandoned; bill_original_paisa; bill_negotiated_paisa) + job_completion (time_spent_mins, labour_rate_paisa snapshot, fuel_paisa, fuel_basis) + job_material (qty × unit_paisa) → 'invoice' posting at CLOSE, on accrual basis only. Close is the first moment the bill is immutable: closed is terminal, and both submit_completion (service.py:1155) and negotiate_bill (service.py:1385) refuse a closed job. Before close, bill edits are operational and post nothing.
- staff_ledger (id; client_id; kind; amount_minor; occurred_on; voided_at/voided_by) + staff_ledger_chain (row_hash of the create/void event) → 'ledger_entry' and 'ledger_reversal'. The chain hash goes into the snapshot as a tamper link.
- advance_request → NO posting of its own. Its money is exactly the one staff_ledger 'advance' row (advance_request.ledger_id). The request id rides in the snapshot so nothing is counted twice. Rejected or failed requests moved no money.
- payroll_export is money-free and produces no postings. job_event and dispatch_cursor are not drawn on.
- External ID = 'fixflow_<kind>_<source_uuid hex32>', with suffix '_x<n>' for the nth reversal and '_r<n>' for revision n ≥ 2. Line IDs are '<move_xid>_l<n>'. Customer partners: 'fixflow_cust_<customer uuid>' when job.customer_id is resolved, else one 'fixflow_cust_walkin' (owner decision on PII to Odoo). Tech partners: 'fixflow_tech_<shop>_<tech_id>'. Never use a seq, token or chain seq: a fresh DB restarts them, and t1..t5/m1 recur (S14, O07-F11).

(2) APPROVAL BOUNDARY (does not exist today)
Table posting:
- id uuid PK; shop_id FK shop.
- seq bigint, per-shop gapless, assigned under pg_advisory_xact_lock(shop) held to commit (the staff_ledger_chain pattern, so it is commit-ordered).
- source_kind CHECK IN (payment, payment_reversal, invoice, ledger_entry, ledger_reversal); source_id uuid; source_rev smallint default 1; UNIQUE (source_kind, source_id, source_rev) is the stager's idempotency key.
- reverses_posting_id uuid FK posting, NULL; CHECK (reversal kind ⇔ NOT NULL); UNIQUE partial (reverses_posting_id) so a posting is reversed at most once.
- external_id varchar(128) UNIQUE NOT NULL.
- accounting_date date (the fact's shop-local date); currency char(3) (snapshot of shop.currency, never a hardcoded 'PKR').
- amount_minor bigint CHECK > 0 (unsigned; direction comes from kind via a code table POSTING_TEMPLATE, the LEDGER_SIGN discipline).
- lines jsonb: [{role, account_code|null, debit_minor, credit_minor, label, partner_xid}], with Σdebit = Σcredit = amount enforced in the service and re-checked by a verify endpoint.
- snapshot jsonb: canonical, PII-free source fields (job token, method, tech_id, ledger kind, chain row_hash, labour/fuel/materials split, original and payable figures, advance_request id). snapshot_hash char(64) = sha256(version‖canonical bytes), using a stdlib-only canonicaliser like attendance/chain.py.
- flags text[]: abandoned, negotiated_below_original, negotiated_stale, post_close_void, void_date_unknown, offline_dated, original_rejected.
- status CHECK IN (staged, approved, rejected, exported, posted, transport_failed).
- staged_at; decided_by FK technician; decided_at.
- reject_code CHECK IN (duplicate, test_entry, not_business, voided_before_posting, covered_by_opening_balance, other); reject_reason varchar(512). CHECK (status <> 'rejected' OR (reject_code IS NOT NULL AND length(btrim(reject_reason)) > 0)).
- export_id FK posting_export NULL; remote_ref varchar(64) NULL; posted_at NULL.
- Enforcement: a BEFORE UPDATE trigger rejects any change to source_*, external_id, accounting_date, currency, amount_minor, snapshot, snapshot_hash or reverses_posting_id, and any change to lines once status ≠ staged. A BEFORE DELETE trigger raises. Status moves only by atomic conditional UPDATE with an allowed-from table (the try_transition pattern): approve staged→approved; reject staged→rejected; export approved→exported; post approved|exported→posted; transport_failed⇄approved. A replay is an idempotent success.

Table posting_decision (append-only): id; posting_id FK; decision IN (approve, reject, restage); actor FK technician; reason_code; reason; client_id UNIQUE; decided_at. Status is the projection of the latest decision. A 'restage' of a rejected row never edits it: it stages a NEW posting at source_rev + 1, with a new external_id, linked through the snapshot. The rejected row stays queryable forever.

Table posting_attempt (append-only): id; posting_id NULL FK; export_id NULL FK; transport IN (csv, odoo_json2); attempt_no; started_at; finished_at; outcome IN (ok, already_present, failed_definitive, ambiguous, auth_failed, rate_limited); http_status; remote_ref; request_sha256; error varchar(1024).

How sources become postings (stager job 'posting-stage-scan': daily, plus an on-demand manager trigger; idempotent; idle until posting_start_date is set; only facts with accounting_date ≥ start):
- Payment: Dr cash_<method>, Cr customer_receipts. The owner maps customer_receipts to a revenue account (cash basis) or to receivable (accrual). A payment is staged even if already voided, so the trail is complete.
- Void: for each voided payment whose payment posting exists and is not yet reversed, stage a payment_reversal with the lines swapped, dated voided_at; if voided_at is NULL, use the staging date and flag void_date_unknown. If the original was rejected, the reversal is still staged and flagged original_rejected, and the manager rejects it with voided_before_posting, so both sides stay visible.
- Bill / invoice (accrual only): every closed job with a bill, abandoned included (flagged; O07-F3). Lines: Dr receivable = payable; Cr revenue_labour; Cr revenue_fuel; Cr revenue_parts (gross original); and a sales_discount line for original − payable on whichever side its sign requires (O07-F4, O07-F9).
- Bill correction: no path today changes a closed bill. If one is ever added (reopen) or a non-rejected posting's source snapshot_hash drifts, stage a reversal of the prior revision plus a new revision. Never update.
- Ledger entry, by kind: earning Dr wages_expense / Cr wages_payable[tech]; adjustment_credit Dr wages_expense / Cr wages_payable; advance Dr staff_advances[tech] / Cr cash_cash; settlement Dr wages_payable / Cr cash_cash; adjustment_debit Dr wages_payable / Cr staff_deductions. The stager first calls attendance verify_ledger_chain and refuses to stage on a verify failure (alarm).
- Advance: covered by its ledger row, as above.
- Poison rows (e.g. amount ≤ 0 under the NOT VALID CHECK from 0038) are skipped with an app_event alarm and counted as 'unpostable' (O07-F8).

Manager step (all routes require_manager): GET /api/postings?status=staged; POST /api/postings/{id}/approve; POST /api/postings/{id}/reject {reason_code, reason} (required); POST /api/postings/approve-window {from, to, expected_count, expected_sum_minor}. Bulk approve needs a single confirmation, and returns 409 if the staged set changed since the manager looked. Approval resolves each role to the account_code_<role> setting and freezes the lines, and is refused (400 naming the role) while a role is unmapped. Rejection is per row and needs a typed reason. So the default path (stage everything, approve all) is full-fidelity, and leaving something out costs per-row effort that leaves a trace.

(3) DEFAULT TRANSPORT: window-keyed CSV for Odoo's importer (works on any plan)
- run_posting_export(shop_id, today) clones run_weekly_export's idempotent record + storage object + manager download, with three fixes. First, the window is over posting.decided_at (approval time) in shop-local dates, so late or back-dated facts go into the next export and keep their own accounting_date (O07-F2). Second, it takes pg_advisory_xact_lock and inserts posting_export first (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING), then claims rows with UPDATE posting SET status='exported', export_id=:id WHERE status='approved' AND export_id IS NULL AND decided_at in window, then writes deterministic bytes (ordered by seq) to accounting/<shop>/<from>_<to>/journal.csv plus manifest.json and manifest.csv, records csv_sha256, and commits; a re-run returns the same record and bytes (O07-F10). Third, export is a scheduler job (weekly, or monthly as the owner chooses) plus on-demand.
- posting_export columns: id; shop_id; window_from; window_to; storage_path; manifest_path; posting_count; move_count; line_count; total_debit_minor; total_credit_minor; csv_sha256; rejected_count; rejected_sum_minor; pending_count; pending_sum_minor; created_at; UNIQUE (shop_id, window_from, window_to).
- CSV (account.move, move_type entry, in Odoo's parent/child import shape; verify the column labels on the owner's version, 20.0 or SaaS 19.x): External ID, Journal, Date, Reference, Journal Items/External ID, Journal Items/Account, Journal Items/Partner, Journal Items/Label, Journal Items/Debit, Journal Items/Credit. The first row of each move carries the move fields; its other line rows leave them blank. Reference = 'FixFlow <kind> job #<token>/<ledger kind> <external_id>'. Amounts are converted from integer minor units at the edge with divmod into a fixed-decimal string (decimal places from currency), never through float. Journals: journal_code_sales / cash / payroll.
- Manifest as separate files (O07-F12): export id; window; posting/move/line counts; Σdebit = Σcredit in minor units; count and sum per kind; csv sha256; first and last posting seq; the window's rejected count and sum by reason_code; and the pending count and sum.
- Idempotency: Odoo's importer updates the record holding an existing External ID (R-02 F10). Line External IDs stop a re-imported draft move from appending lines. Re-importing an already-posted move should fail loudly rather than duplicate (verify in the test company).
- Acknowledgement: after import the manager calls POST /api/postings/exports/{id}/imported, which moves postings exported→posted and writes a posting_attempt with transport csv and outcome ok. GET /api/postings/exports returns signed URLs (mint_playback_url) through the existing storage abstraction, R2 or self-hosted.

(4) OPTIONAL TRANSPORT: JSON-2 behind a Protocol (Custom plan only, S15)
- core/posting_transport.py: async Protocol PostingTransport { name; async find(external_id) -> RemoteRef|None; async push(snapshot) -> RemoteRef }, with typed DefinitiveTransportError, AmbiguousTransportError and TransportAuthError. idempotency_key = external_id. It mirrors PaymentRail's narrow-surface contract but is async (O07-F13).
- Default CsvExportTransport: push is a no-op, the export is the transport. OdooJson2Transport is configured by FIXFLOW_ODOO_URL, FIXFLOW_ODOO_DB (sent as the X-Odoo-Database header) and FIXFLOW_ODOO_API_KEY (an env secret, never a shop_setting), and authenticates as a dedicated minimal-rights bot user. It never uses /xmlrpc or /jsonrpc (deprecated, removal in Odoo 22).
- Worker: scheduler job 'erp-push', gated by settings.enable_erp_push (default OFF), single replica. Each tick selects approved|exported, not-posted postings ORDER BY seq. A reversal waits until its original is posted.
- Per posting: (a) search-before-create: /json/2/account.move/search_read with domain ref = external_id (or ir.model.data module 'fixflow' + name); a hit means attempt outcome already_present, then mark posted. (b) Otherwise create in ONE call that carries the External ID: prefer account.move/load with an 'id' column (the importer's semantics), or else create with ref = external_id. Never split create and the xid link across two calls, because each JSON-2 call is its own transaction (R-02 F5). (c) action_post only if the owner chooses; the default leaves moves in draft for review in Odoo.
- Budget: a token bucket at 1 call per second, serial, no parallel calls. Chunk load() calls of up to about 50 moves.
- Failure handling: ambiguous (timeout, 5xx, connection) halts the tick, and the next tick re-searches. Definitive 4xx (e.g. unknown account) marks the posting transport_failed with a visible error and halts the queue by default. 401/403 halts and raises the 'erp_auth_failed' alarm. Every call writes a posting_attempt row.
- Key rotation: keys last at most three months (R-02 F3). The owner records odoo_api_key_expires_on; ops deep-health turns degraded and writes an app_event 21 days before expiry; rotation is manual (new key, env, setting). Programmatic res.users.apikeys.generate needs admin rights or a system parameter and is not the default.
- Lag alert: oldest approved-not-posted older than posting_lag_alert_hours (default 48), or oldest staged-undecided older than 7 days, shows on the ops deep-health surface plus an app_event. No pull from Odoo except remote_ref.

(5) RECONCILIATION VIEW
GET /api/postings/reconciliation?from&to (manager), per kind, over accounting_date:
- Operational totals use the stager's predicates, read straight from the source tables: Σ non-voided job_payment by method; Σ payable of closed jobs; Σ non-voided staff_ledger by kind, signed with LEDGER_SIGN.
- Projection totals: staged, approved, exported and posted, net of reversals.
- Delta = operational − posted, itemised as: unstaged (should be 0; non-zero means stager lag or a bug); unpostable (with source ids); pending decision; rejected by reason_code (count, sum, reason texts, actor); approved-not-exported; exported-not-acknowledged; transport_failed.
- Informational lines: negotiated discounts (original − payable) by actor; abandoned-with-bill totals; payments on jobs not yet closed; post-close voids; voids by actor.
- The rejected-sum line is shown first, and the same figure is printed on each export manifest. This is 'the cost of informality made visible' (BACKEND-REQUIREMENTS 3.15).
